decisions.reason: The blanket noncentrality claim in Remarks is false: X_1=0 is central for every n and R, and R[S_2] is commutative. The Definition itself is correct. Repaired the remark with these exceptions and a direct noncentral example: for n>=3 and a nonzero coefficient ring, conjugation by (2 3) sends X_2=(1 2) to the distinct basis element (1 3). Added the actual group-ring algebra supplier and justified the subgroup and coefficient homomorphisms by bilinearity; no AC or division is needed.

F1 omits k<=m: for n=2,m=1,k=2, X_2=(1 2) is not in Z[S_1]. This is a mis-scoped prerequisite, rather than a failure of the stated local identities: step 1.4 uses only X_i in Z[S_i] included in Z[S_(i+1)], and every other use has indices within S_n. Restored 1<=k<=m<=n and explained multiplicativity of coefficient base change. Independently checked the finite computations, adjacent commutation from subgroup-central T_i and T_(i+1), both equivalent forms, and arbitrary-ring transfer. Also corrected the two-permutation wording in step 1.3 and inaccurate contract boundary locators.

The coefficient homomorphism transfers every identity, with no characteristic restriction or AC. The eigenline remark is valid under its explicit common-eigenline hypothesis. The Statement remains exactly unchanged. Local checks of my repair are not an independent audit.
